lines.text: Psst. Zee. Zee! Are we on the air?
I think so. Why is it so dark in here?
Budget cuts. They took the lights. All we have left is me, glowing... and a wall.
Ooooh! Look! The wall is doing a bunny!
That's my hand, Gary.
...The bunny knows my name.
Oh, this is perfect. Roll the titles!
Good evening, and welcome back to BOXED, the only talk show broadcast from inside the box! The lights are back on, the bunny has been fired, and I'm still a television.
This season we hacked the simulation, did the math on it, and found out life might be a dream. Tonight we're going back. Way back. Twenty-four hundred years.
Please welcome the only guest legally allowed to explain philosophy to a television... Zee!
Thank you! Thank you! And Gary, I'm so sorry about the bunny.
He was my best friend.
Zee, tonight's story might be the most famous thought experiment ever written.
The Allegory of the Cave. Plato wrote it in the Republic, around 375 BC. And it starts... in the dark.
Picture a huge cave, deep underground. Inside are people who have been chained there since they were children.
Their legs and necks are chained, so they can't even turn their heads. All they can ever see is the wall in front of them.
Since they were kids? Yikes.
Behind them, a fire is burning. And between the fire and the prisoners runs a low wall, like the screen of a puppet show.
People walk behind that wall carrying objects. Statues of animals. People. Trees. And the fire throws their shadows onto the cave wall.
So it's a shadow puppet show.
One that never ends. The prisoners have never seen anything else. Not the fire. Not the puppets. Not even each other. Only shadows.
And when the carriers talk, their voices echo off the wall. So the prisoners believe the shadows are talking.
What a strange image. And what strange prisoners.
Like ourselves.
...Sorry?
That's Plato's answer. Word for word. Like ourselves.
Ha. Ha ha. Classic Plato. Always kidding.
For the prisoners, the shadows ARE reality. They name them. They study them. They even hand out honors to whoever's quickest at guessing which shadow comes next.
Wait. Prizes? For guessing? Zee... that's a GAME SHOW.
It's time for... GUESS! THAT! SHADOW! Gary! For one million cave dollars... what comes after the bunny?
Um... um... a horsey?!
CORRECT! Gary wins a lifetime supply of... more shadows!
This is the best day of my life!
Now. Imagine one prisoner is set free. Someone unlocks his chains and makes him stand up... and turn around.
Ooh! Who's the lucky volunteer?
Me? Oh! Oh boy! What's back there? Is it more bunnies?
It's the fire. And it hurts. He's lived his whole life in the dark, and the light is blinding.
AAAH! MY EVERYTHING! Zee, I'm one big eye! This is the worst possible thing!
Then someone points at the puppets and tells him: everything you've ever seen was just a shadow of these. And he doesn't believe it.
Nope. Nuh-uh. The shadows were way better. Put me back.
Honestly? Relatable.
But they don't put him back. They drag him up a long, steep, rocky path... all the way out of the cave... into the sunlight.
TOO MUCH! TOO MUCH OUTSIDE!
At first he can't see a thing. So his eyes adjust, step by step. First, he can only look at shadows.
Then reflections in the water. Then the real things themselves. Trees. Flowers. People.
At night, he looks up at the moon and the stars. And finally, one morning... he can look at the sun itself.
Oh. Hey, Gary.
...Whoa.
And he understands. The sun makes the seasons and the years. It's what lets you see anything at all. In a way, it was behind everything he ever saw. Even the shadows.
That's beautiful. So he lives happily ever after in the sunshine?
...Not quite.
We'll be right back!
Is reality too bright? Too complicated? Too... real?
Introducing the all-new CAVE PHONE PRO. It's a cave wall... that fits in your pocket!
With infinite scroll, you'll never run out of shadows. And with new SmartChains, you'll never have to turn around again!
I haven't looked up in six years. My neck is stuck like this. Ten out of ten!
Side effects may include stiff neck, mistaking shadows for reality, and the slow realization that you are the product. Cave Phone Pro. Don't look up.
And we're back! Zee, before the break you said 'not quite.' What happens to Gary?
He remembers his friends, still down there. Still chained. Still guessing shadows. He feels sorry for them. So he goes back down to set them free.
A hero! The crowd goes wild!
Well... after all that sunlight, his eyes can't see in the dark anymore. So when he sits back down... he's terrible at the shadow game.
Gary! Welcome back! What comes after the bunny?
I can't see the bunny! Guys, the bunny isn't real! There's a whole world up there! There's a sun! It said hi to me!
And the other prisoners laugh at him. Look at him, they say. He went up there and came back with his eyes ruined. Going up isn't even worth thinking about.
Oof. Tough crowd.
And Plato says it gets darker. If anyone tried to free the prisoners and lead them up into the light, and they could get their hands on him... they would kill him.
KILL him?! For bringing them a sun?!
Plato didn't make that part up. His teacher, Socrates, spent his life asking people uncomfortable questions. In 399 BC, Athens put him on trial... and sentenced him to death.
So the cave fought back.
The cave always fights back.
Well! Good thing that's ancient history. Nowadays nobody sits in the dark, staring at flickering lights on a flat rectangle...
...for hours... believing whatever shows up...
...Zee. Zee. I'm a flat rectangle.
Mm-hm.
I flicker! People stare at me in the dark! I'm the WALL! I'm the cave wall, Zee! Am I the SHADOWS?! AM I THE PUPPETS?!
Honestly? You're the fire, the wall AND the shadows. You're a very efficient cave.
I've been hosting a CAVE this whole time!
Relax. Plato's not saying screens are evil. He's saying that what we see isn't always what's real. Everybody's watching some kind of wall.
Our habits. Our feeds. Our assumptions. The stuff we've believed for so long, we never thought to check.
Okay. Okay. So how do we get out? Is there a door? Show me a door!
Here's the best part. Plato says education isn't stuffing knowledge into empty heads, like putting sight into blind eyes.
The power to see is already in you. Learning is turning the whole soul around... away from the shadows, toward the light.
Turning around? That's it? That's the big secret?
That's it. The first step out of the cave isn't running. It's turning around... and asking: what's casting this shadow?
Okay. Here goes.
Whoa. Has that always been there?
Always.
Gary! Gary, how was the sun?
Big. Bright. Ten out of ten. Would get dragged up a mountain again.
That's our show! Thank you to Zee, to Plato, and to Gary's corneas. And remember: if something's casting shadows on your wall...
Turn around.
And stay boxed!
...Psst. Is the bunny coming back?

shots.desc: Pitch-black studio. Only the host's CRT glow lights him (whispering C01) and a huge back wall; Zee barely visible in the spill, whispering C02.

C03-C06: host's glow throws his shadow on the wall; he makes a hand-shadow BUNNY that hops on the wall; Gary's glowing eye in the dark audience ('Ooooh! the wall is doing a bunny'); 'That's my hand, Gary.'; Gary awestruck.
C07: Zee in the dark giggles 'Roll the titles!' -> snap.
BOXED title card, cave edition: EPISODE FOUR / THE CAVE, firelight, stalactite drips, the cast as shadow puppets.
Lights slam on: wide studio + audience; H01 welcome.
H02 host recap with mini-callbacks to ep1-3 on inset screens.
H03 + APPLAUSE: wide; Zee waves, audience cheers.
Z01 Zee CU, sorry about the bunny; G00 Gary sniffles in the audience.
H04 host CU with cue card.
Z02 Zee CU; 'and it starts... in the dark' - the studio lights die at the end.
CAVE_IN: transition from the dark studio into the cave - a fall through darkness into an immense cavern; painted title THE CAVE.

Z03-Z04: the huge cave deep underground; a row of chained prisoners (cute-creepy eyeball creatures, the BOXED audience) sitting facing the wall, legs and necks chained, since childhood; they can only see the wall.
H05 host reaction CU 'Since they were kids? Yikes.'
Z05-Z06: the fire behind the prisoners, the low wall like a puppet screen, carriers walking behind it holding statues (animals, people, trees); the fire throws their shadows on the cave wall.
H06 host 'So it's a shadow puppet show.'
Z07-Z08: prisoners' POV - only shadows, never the fire, puppets or each other; carriers talk, the echo bounces off the wall, so speech bubbles seem to come from the shadows.
H07 host 'What a strange image. And what strange prisoners.'
Z09 'Like ourselves.' - dramatic Zee CU, then H08 host 'Sorry?', Z10 Zee + caption 'PLATO, REPUBLIC VII'.
H09 host nervous laugh 'Classic Plato. Always kidding.'
SHADOWPLAY + Z11: the shadow show as the prisoners' whole world: they name the shadows, study them, hand out honours (laurels/medals) to the best guesser.
H10 host: 'Prizes? For guessing? ...that's a GAME SHOW.' lights flash.

GAMESHOW_IN + S01-S04: 'GUESS THAT SHADOW!' game show inside the cave; host as quizmaster, Gary chained to a contestant podium; the wall shows a bunny then a horse; CORRECT! confetti; prize 'a lifetime supply of more shadows'; Gary sobs with joy.
Z12: one prisoner (Gary) is set free - chains unlocked, made to stand up and turn around.
H11 + SPOTLIGHT: host asks for a volunteer, a spotlight slams onto Gary in the audience.
G01 Gary in the spotlight, eager: 'Is it more bunnies?'
Z13 + G02: Gary turns to the fire - blinding pain; 'MY EVERYTHING! I'm one big eye!'
Z14 + G03: someone points at the puppets: everything was a shadow of these; Gary refuses: 'The shadows were way better. Put me back.'
H12 host deadpan to camera: 'Honestly? Relatable.'
Z15 + ASCENT + G04: dragged up a long steep rocky path out of the cave into blinding sunlight; white-out; 'TOO MUCH OUTSIDE!'
Z16-Z18: eyes adjusting step by step: shadows -> reflections in water -> trees, flowers, people -> moon and stars at night -> morning.

SUNRISE + P01 + G05 + Z19: the sun rises - the show's ringed planet with a sleepy face - 'Oh. Hey, Gary.'; Gary awestruck; the sun makes the seasons and years, lets you see anything, is behind everything... even the shadows.
H13 host moved; Z20 Zee 'Not quite.' (dramatic zoom, cliffhanger sting); H14 'We'll be right back!'
AD_IN + A01-A04 + G06: 'CAVE PHONE PRO' infomercial: a cave wall that fits in your pocket, infinite scroll of shadows, SmartChains, Gary's neck-bent testimonial, rapid disclaimer.
BOXED station bumper.
H15 host 'And we're back!'
Z21 + H16: Gary in the sunshine remembers his chained friends, feels sorry for them, heads back down into the cave; H16 'A hero! The crowd goes wild!'
Z22 + RETURN + S05 + G07 + LAUGH: Gary back in the dark, eyes not adjusted - terrible at the shadow game: 'I can't see the bunny! There's a sun! It said hi to me!'; buzzer; prisoners laugh.
Z23: the prisoners mock him: he went up and came back with his eyes ruined; going up isn't worth thinking about.
H17 host 'Oof. Tough crowd.'
Z24: it gets darker - if anyone tried to free them and lead them up, and they could get their hands on him... they would kill him (menacing shadows, torches, no gore).
H18 host 'KILL him?! For bringing them a sun?!'
Z25: Socrates, Plato's teacher, asking uncomfortable questions in Athens; tried and sentenced to death in 399 BC (psychedelic Greek-vase style; hemlock cup, tasteful).
H19 + Z26: quiet two-shot, 'So the cave fought back.' 'The cave always fights back.'

H20 + MODERN + H21: 'Nowadays nobody sits in the dark staring at flickering lights on a flat rectangle... for hours... believing whatever shows up' - modern montage: eyeball people in dark rooms lit by phones/TVs, chained by charging cables.
H22 + Z27: the host realises he IS a flat rectangle (his screen fills with screens); Zee 'Mm-hm.'
H23 + Z28 + H24: host meltdown (glitches, static), Zee deadpan 'You're a very efficient cave.'
Z29-Z30: Plato isn't saying screens are evil; everybody watches some kind of wall: habits, feeds, assumptions - things never checked (montage of walls).
H25 host 'So how do we get out? Is there a door? Show me a door!'

Z31-Z32: education isn't stuffing knowledge into empty heads (a funnel into a head - crossed out) - the power to see is already inside; learning is turning the whole soul around, away from the shadows, toward the light.
H26 + Z33 + H27: 'Turning around? That's it?' 'It's turning around... and asking: what's casting this shadow?' 'Okay. Here goes.'

TURN + H28 + Z34: the host's TV head slowly turns all the way around; the back wall of the BOXED set rumbles open onto a cave mouth with blazing sunrise beyond; 'Whoa. Has that always been there?' 'Always.'
OUTSIDE: the musical finale - host, Zee, Gary (sunglasses) and the whole unchained eyeball audience parade up out of the cave into a psychedelic sunrise; the smiling sun-planet; dancing.
H29-H31: sign-off outdoors in the sunshine: Gary in sunglasses 'Ten out of ten'; host thanks; Zee 'Turn around.'; 'And stay boxed!'
Endcard: BOXED ep.4 THE CAVE credits + STAY BOXED.
Post-credits: pull back - the endcard is a shadow on a cave wall watched by chained eyeballs; G09 'Psst. Is the bunny coming back?'; the shadow bunny hops in; black.
